thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER | cross-region routing anomalies detected. sudden surge of eu->apac steering decisions since 5965431800. affected zones: eu-west-1, eu-central-1. symptoms: increased tail latency for eu traffic, ~25% traffic shifted to apac, customer errors 502/504. dashboards: https://grafana.internal/redwood/routing?panel=latency-steer . please ack and join #incidents-call if needed

Eric (oncall): acked. i'm pulling routing decision logs and policy history. did a policy rollout happen ~5m ago? tagging @Lina (netops)

Lina (netops): i pushed a latency-steering rule at 5965431700 (commit 9f3b2c). the change lowered the latency threshold for eu->apac failover from 220ms to 150ms to try to reduce eu tail latency. rollout was gradual (5% -> 50% -> 100%) but looks like some edge caches honored the 5% early and amplified decisions. rolling back now if we confirm impact.

Jamal (infra): pulling router logs and sampling decisions. looks like a decision amplification loop: CDN+edge cached the routing header and forwarded subsequent requests with the new header, causing regional affinity to flip. sample log:```
[5965431897] decision id=dec-7742 shard=router-eu-3 input_latency=155ms selected_region=apac1 reason=latency-threshold-hit policy=latency-9f3b2c
[5965431902] decision id=dec-7743 shard=router-eu-3 input_latency=148ms selected_region=apac1 reason=cached-header
```
we also see TTLs on the routing header (x-rw-region-ttl) set to 60s in some proxies, which keeps the misroute sticky beyond the policy change.

DeployBot: policy rollout detected: commit 9f3b2c applied to fleets: router-eu-*-prod at 5965431700. Rollout status: COMPLETED -> 100% at 5965431785.

Eric (oncall): ok we have a cause: aggressive threshold + cached routing header = amplification. mitigation plan: 1) rollback policy 9f3b2c (stop steering) 2) issue a short-lived pin override to force eu routing for affected customer prefixes 3) flush/expire routing-header cache on edge proxies where possible 4) notify CS for impacted customers. Lina/Jamal please take 1-3. Alice/Zara handle 4.

Lina (netops): rolling back commit 9f3b2c now. running command:```
/rwctl policies rollback --commit=9f3b2c --env=prod --confirm
```
will watch traffic. estimated 30s to propagate to control plane and 2-5 minutes for decision stream to stabilize.

Jamal (infra): applying pin override for affected prefixes:```
/rwctl pin set --region=eu-west-1 --selector="customer:high-traffic,route:public" --ttl=300 --note="mitigate misroute 5965432100"
```
also sending a purge to edge caches for header key `x-rw-region` where supported:```
curl -X POST https://edge-api.internal/purge -d '{"key":"x-rw-region" , "prefix":"/api/"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer ****"
```
note: some third-party CDNs don't support purge, so their cached headers will expire naturally (TTL 60s).

RouterBot: rollback initiated for commit 9f3b2c by Lina. control-plane ack=5965432175.

DeployBot: rollback completed at 5965432205. policy state: previous commit restored (commit 72a1ab).

Jamal (infra): we're seeing decision ratios moving back: eu->apac down from 62% to 8% in last 45s. 95th latency for eu services trending back to baseline. logs sample:```
[5965432230] decision id=dec-7820 shard=router-eu-3 input_latency=165ms selected_region=eu-west-1 reason=policy-default
```

Alice (PM): what's the customer impact window? any paid customers hit 5xx spikes?

Zara (CS): preliminary list: customers with heavy eu traffic and long polling: AcmeCorp, LumiApps, BridgeX. AcmeCorp reported timeouts from monitoring at 5965431850 -> they opened a support ticket. I'm drafting a heads-up note: "We detected a transient routing anomaly that briefly routed EU traffic to APAC; we mitigated by rolling back a routing policy and expect no lasting data loss." will send to impacted contacts.

Eric (oncall): opening incident ticket: INC-596543 | severity=sev2 (customer-facing errors on multiple customers). joincall: https://meet.internal/5965432100 . tagging pager for handoff in 30m if still active.

Lina (netops): one more action: will push a hotfix to set x-rw-region TTL to 5s in proxies to reduce stickiness for future experiments -> patching config now.

Jamal (infra): pushed header-ttl override to proxies (config-change id cfg-441). monitoring for regressions.

RouterBot: control-plane telemetry shows reduced amplification after header-ttl change. metric: routing-affinity-amplification dropped from 3.2x -> 1.05x.

Eric (oncall): current status: rollback complete, pin overrides in place (TTL=300), header TTL reduced to 5s, traffic normalized. marking incident as "mitigated". we'll run a postmortem. Lina/Jamal — please capture exact timeline and root cause (policy change + edge caching behavior). Alice/Zara — coordinate customer comms and include timelines.

Zara (CS): sent notifications to impacted customers at 5965432350. sample note: "We observed a brief routing issue affecting EU traffic between 12:22 and 12:26 UTC; traffic has been restored. We're investigating root cause and will follow up"

Eric (oncall): handing off to Lina for follow-up analysis. I'll stay available for 15 more minutes then hand pager to next oncall. Lina, please update the incident channel once you have the timeline and if you want a postmortem.

Lina (netops): ack. will post full timeline + impacted CIDR list and proposed prevention steps (policy rollout gating, experiment guardrails, header ttl defaults).

Jamal (infra): creating playbook note: "latency-steer rollout checklist" to add: probe for header caching behavior, set conservative header TTLs, rollback quick path.

RouterBot: incident marked mitigated at 5965432380 by Eric.

Eric (oncall): last checks looking good. closing pager but leaving channel open for follow-ups. thanks all for quick response :thumbsup:
